title: Molecular Polarity Dipole Moment Calculator
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive 3D molecular polarity and dipole moment calculator. The scene serves as an educational chemistry tool where users build molecules from atoms, visualize bond dipoles, and compute the net molecular dipole moment vector.

## Scene Setup
- Use a dark background (0x1a1a2e) with a perspective camera at position (0, 5, 12) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two directional lights: one from (5, 10, 5) intensity 0.8, one from (-5, -5, 10) intensity 0.3.
- Add OrbitControls for camera rotation/zoom.
- Draw a subtle grid helper (size 20, divisions 20, color 0x333355) on the XZ plane.
- Load the asset 'WaterBottle.glb' using GLTFLoader and place it at position (6, 0, -4) scaled to 2.0 as a decorative lab prop. Store a reference so its visibility can be toggled.

## Molecule System
- Maintain a list of atoms. Each atom has: id (integer), element symbol (string), position (THREE.Vector3), electronegativity (float), mesh (THREE.Mesh sphere).
- Maintain a list of bonds. Each bond connects two atom IDs and is rendered as a cylinder between them.
- Pre-define electronegativity values: H=2.20, C=2.55, N=3.04, O=3.44, F=3.98, Cl=3.16, Br=2.96, S=2.58.
- Atoms are rendered as color-coded spheres: H=white(0xffffff) radius 0.3, C=gray(0x555555) radius 0.5, N=blue(0x3333ff) radius 0.48, O=red(0xff3333) radius 0.46, F=green(0x33ff33) radius 0.35, Cl=green(0x00cc00) radius 0.55, Br=darkred(0x993300) radius 0.6, S=yellow(0xffff00) radius 0.52.

## Bond Dipole Calculation
- For each bond between atoms A and B, compute the bond dipole magnitude as |EN_A - EN_B| (electronegativity difference).
- The bond dipole vector points FROM the less electronegative atom TOWARD the more electronegative atom, with magnitude = |EN_A - EN_B|.
- Visualize each bond dipole as an arrow (THREE.ArrowHelper) colored cyan (0x00ffff) along the bond, pointing toward the more electronegative atom.
- The net molecular dipole moment is the vector sum of all bond dipole vectors. Visualize it as a large magenta (0xff00ff) arrow from the geometric center of the molecule.

## Preset Molecules
- Provide 4 preset molecules loaded via buttons:
  1. 'Water (H2O)': O at (0,0,0), H at (0.76, 0.59, 0), H at (-0.76, 0.59, 0). Bonds: O-H, O-H. Expected net dipole magnitude ~1.76 (approx).
  2. 'Carbon Dioxide (CO2)': C at (0,0,0), O at (1.16, 0, 0), O at (-1.16, 0, 0). Bonds: C-O, C-O. Expected net dipole ~0 (linear, cancels).
  3. 'Ammonia (NH3)': N at (0, 0.37, 0), H at (0.94, -0.12, 0), H at (-0.47, -0.12, 0.81), H at (-0.47, -0.12, -0.81). Bonds: N-H, N-H, N-H.
  4. 'Hydrogen Fluoride (HF)': H at (-0.46, 0, 0), F at (0.46, 0, 0). Bond: H-F.
- A 'Clear All' button removes all atoms, bonds, and arrows.

## User Interactions
- A dropdown select element (id='elementSelect') lets the user pick an element: H, C, N, O, F, Cl, Br, S.
- An 'Add Atom' button (id='btnAddAtom') places the selected element at a random position within radius 3 of origin on the XZ plane (y=0).
- Clicking on two atoms sequentially (using raycasting on click) selects them (highlight with emissive yellow 0xffff00). When two atoms are selected, a 'Create Bond' button (id='btnCreateBond') becomes enabled. Clicking it creates a bond between them, deselects both, and recalculates all dipoles.
- A 'Toggle Dipole Arrows' button (id='btnToggleDipoles') shows/hides all bond dipole arrows and the net dipole arrow.
- A 'Toggle Lab Prop' button (id='btnToggleProp') toggles visibility of the WaterBottle.glb model.
- Keyboard: pressing 'R' recalculates and refreshes all dipole vectors. Pressing 'Delete' removes the last added atom and any bonds connected to it.

## HUD / UI Panel
- A fixed panel on the left side (width 300px, semi-transparent dark background) containing:
  - Title: 'Dipole Moment Calculator'
  - The element dropdown and Add Atom button
  - Preset molecule buttons (ids: 'btnWater', 'btnCO2', 'btnNH3', 'btnHF')
  - Create Bond button
  - Toggle Dipole Arrows button
  - Toggle Lab Prop button
  - Clear All button (id='btnClearAll')
  - A readout div (id='dipoleReadout') showing: number of atoms, number of bonds, net dipole vector (x, y, z) rounded to 2 decimals, net dipole magnitude rounded to 4 decimals.
  - A polarity classification label (id='polarityLabel'): 'Nonpolar' if net dipole magnitude < 0.05, 'Weakly Polar' if < 0.5, 'Polar' if < 2.0, 'Highly Polar' if >= 2.0.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose and continuously update:
- atomCount (int): number of atoms currently in scene
- bondCount (int): number of bonds
- atoms (array of {id, element, x, y, z, electronegativity})
- bonds (array of {atomA_id, atomB_id, dipoleMagnitude, dipoleVector: {x,y,z}})
- netDipole: {x, y, z} the net dipole vector components (floats)
- netDipoleMagnitude (float): magnitude of net dipole
- polarityClass (string): 'Nonpolar'|'Weakly Polar'|'Polar'|'Highly Polar'
- selectedAtomIds (array of int): currently selected atom IDs (0, 1, or 2 elements)
- dipolesVisible (bool): whether dipole arrows are shown
- labPropVisible (bool): whether WaterBottle.glb is visible
- currentPreset (string): name of last loaded preset or 'custom'
- lastAction (string): description of last user action

Recalculate all dipole data whenever atoms or bonds change. Ensure all numerical values are NaN-free.
physics_constraints: Bond dipole vectors must point from less electronegative to more electronegative atom with magnitude equal to the absolute electronegativity difference. Net molecular dipole must be the exact vector sum of all bond dipoles. CO2 must yield near-zero net dipole due to linear symmetry cancellation. All vectors must be NaN-free and magnitudes must be non-negative.
